headline: Tiny Frog on Brink of Extinction Breeds Successfully in Care
meta_description: A critically endangered frog species found only in two pools in Ghana has been bred in human care for the first time, offering hope against mining threats.
summary_short: Fifteen 5mm froglets of the Afia Birago's puddle frog have been born in captivity—a breakthrough for a species found nowhere else on Earth.
body:
A frog species so rare it exists in just two pools in Ghana has been bred under human care for the first time. Fifteen Afia Birago's puddle froglets—each a mere 5mm long—were born at Londo, marking a turning point for one of the world's most endangered amphibians.

The tiny frogs face an uncertain future in their native habitat, where mining threatens the very pools they depend on to survive. With their range limited to these two small pools in Ghana, the species exists on a razor's edge: one environmental disaster could push them toward extinction.

The successful captive breeding offers a lifeline. These microscopic newborns represent not just genetic continuity, but proof that the species can reproduce outside its native environment—a crucial backup should conservation efforts in Ghana falter. For a frog that has nowhere else to go, human care may be the bridge that saves it.
quick_facts: Afia Birago's puddle frog found only in two pools in Ghana
15 froglets born in captivity, each 5mm long
Mining poses direct threat to their habitat
First successful breeding under human care
